thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Gains Ground As Energy, Tech Sectors Lead

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Gains Ground As Energy, Tech Sectors Lead

organizations.name: stock market gains ground as energy

text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Dow posts triple-digit rise
U.S. stocks rose Tuesday, with the Dow climbing by triple digits, as energy shares rallied and the technology sector extended gains. Shares had been wobbly earlier as unresolved trade issues continued to dog the market.
Where are the major benchmarks trading?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 133 points, or 0.5%, to 25,992. The S&P 500 added 13 points, or 0.5%, to 2,890 with energy, technology and telecom sectors leading the gains. The tech-laden Nasdaq Composite Index advanced 50 points, or 0.6%, to 7,975.
What's driving the market?
The energy sector was the best performer on the back of strong crude oil prices while tech shares were among notable gainers with megacaps Apple Inc. (AAPL), Facebook Inc. (FB) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) all rallying.
However, trade worries were simmering below the surface as investors continued to watch the situation between the U.S. and China after President Donald Trump recently threatened China with fresh tariffs. The latest move by Trump would impact an additional $267 billion in Chinese goods, coming on top of an already-proposed $200 billion in tariffs.
China has vowed to retaliate and plans to ask the World Trade Organization next week for permission to impose sanctions on the U.S. for Washington's noncompliance with a ruling in a dispute over U.S. dumping duties, Reuters reported (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-china-sanctions/china-asks-wto-for-sanctions-in-u-s-trade-dispute-idUSKCN1LR0TM). That's part of a dispute that goes back to 2013.
Investors are worried about a full-on trade war that could have negative implications for global economic growth.
EU and U.S. negotiators met Monday to talk over a pact (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-eu-negotiators-cite-progress-in-latest-discussions-over-trade-2018-09-11)that would avoid a trans-Atlantic spat. Although there was no major breakthrough, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and European Trade Commissioner Cecilia Malmström said they would meet up again by the end of September and begin hammering out a deal in the coming months.
Investors are also facing negative seasonal issues, as the month of September is historically the weakest of the year, with an average loss of 1.05% since 1896.
Opinion: Resist the urge to sell if another 9/11-scale attack sinks the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/resist-the-urge-to-sell-if-another-911-scale-attack-sinks-the-stock-market-2018-09-11)
What are strategists saying?
Mike Antonelli, an equity sales trader at Robert W. Baird & Co., credited some of the turnaround to an "oversold bounce" as investors returned to the market to look for bargains after the market's recent losing streak.
The stock market recovered on the back of higher oil prices, which revived interest in the energy sector, according to Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management. Oil futures were up 2.5%.
"You have to watch the trade issue because global supply chains are so complex, and economic growth has depend on the efficiency of these chains," said Tom Plumb, chief investment officer of Plumb Funds.
"Having said that, people talk about the trade issue as though nothing will happen, or as though the worst-case scenario will happen. We think it will be somewhere in between, and while I would stay away from emerging markets and China for a while, we have so much momentum in the U.S. that I would expect any correction to be short lived," he said.
Plumb said he was using the recent weakness as an opportunity to buy stocks like Apple. "Any opportunity to have to buy this at a discount, you'll be well served this year and next," he said.
Which stocks are in focus?
Yum China Holdings Inc. (YUMC) sank 13% after Bloomberg reported that Hillhouse Capital was dropping its pursuit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/yum-chinas-stock-plunges-to-pace-nyse-decliners-after-report-suitor-has-dropped-interest-2018-09-11) of operator of Pizza Hut and KFC fast-food restaurants in China.
Shares of Integrated Device Technology Inc.(IDTI) surged 11% after Japan's Renesas Electronics Corp. said it would buy the California-based chip maker in a $6.7 billion deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/integrated-device-technology-scooped-up-by-japans-renesas-for-67-billion-2018-09-11).
Sonos Inc. shares sank 21% after the speaker maker's first earnings report since its initial public offering (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sonos-stock-gives-back-some-of-its-record-gains-after-first-earnings-since-ipo-2018-09-10) showed a net loss and sales that were worse than those reported in the same quarter a year ago. The speaker maker's stock had rallied into the release, soaring 13% in Monday's session.
Tesla Inc. (TSLA) fell 2.5% after it was downgraded by an analyst (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/teslas-stock-drops-after-elon-musks-erratic-behavior-prompts-downgrade-2018-09-11) who cited the "erratic behavior" of Chief Executive Elon Musk.
Sonic Corp.(SONC) surged 9.5% after the fast-food restaurant chain gave an outlook that was above expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sonics-stock-rallies-after-upbeat-profit-sales-outlook-2018-09-11).
Francesca's Holdings Corp.(FRAN) tumbled 32% and hit all-time lows after the women's clothing chain reported fiscal second-quarter earnings and sales that missed expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/francescas-stock-plunges-toward-record-low-after-profit-and-sales-miss-downbeat-outlook-2018-09-11), and provided a downbeat outlook, citing "weak traffic trends."
MasTec Inc.(MTZ) said it had authorized a new $150 million stock repurchase program (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mastec-sets-new-150-million-stock-buyback-program-2018-09-11), the largest in the infrastructure construction company's history. Shares came off earlier highs to edge up 0.1%.
Which economic reports are in focus?
Small-business sentiment climbed to a record in August (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/small-business-sentiment-reaches-new-record-in-august-nfib-says-2018-09-11), according to the National Federation of Independent Business.
Separately, the number of job openings in the U.S. climbed to a record 6.94 million in July (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-job-openings-climb-to-record-69-million-2018-09-11) while the U.S. budget deficit in August was $211 billion, nearly double the gap during the year-ago period (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-budget-deficit-widens-to-fifth-highest-ever-cbo-reports-2018-09-11).
What are other markets doing?
Stocks in Asia had a weak day (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-jumps-but-other-asian-markets-remain-sluggish-2018-09-10) with the Hang Seng retreating to drag the Hong Kong market into bear territory. European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/europe-stocks-struggle-with-ftse-100-dragged-by-pound-strength-2018-09-11) were also mostly lower.
Gold settled slightly higher and the dollar index was flat.
--Barbara Kollmeyer contributed to this report
(END) Dow Jones Newswires
